title: Runtime config apply/rollback: atomic update semantics + locking/lease to prevent concurrent applies
creator: Mateo Alvarez
content:
Overview
We need runtime-side guarantees that applying an Optimize config version (and rolling back) is (a) atomic per scope and (b) serialized so we never have multiple concurrent applies fighting each other (split-brain). This ticket defines the locking/lease behavior and the runtime activation semantics used by control plane apply/rollback.

Context
Safe apply + rollback adds version history and a control-plane workflow. This ticket covers the runtime integration contract:
- Atomic activation per scope (no mixed knobs within a scope)
- Deterministic “active version” pointer per scope
- Locking/lease to prevent concurrent apply/rollback for the same scope
- Status reporting and failure semantics so Console can show progress + unblock rollback under partial failures

Scope and terminology
Scope key (what we serialize on)
We will lock on a normalized scope key composed of:
- deployment_type: hosted | dedicated | private
- tenant_id (or internal customer_id)
- environment: prod | staging | sandbox
- region
- cluster_id
- route_id (or route_name)
- model_id (catalog model or customer-pinned model)

Rationale: apply/rollback is per route+model+tenant+region/cluster. Locking at this level prevents overlapping updates in the exact blast radius while still allowing parallel applies across unrelated scopes.

Non-goals
- Cross-scope transactionality (e.g., apply simultaneously across multiple regions). That’s handled by rollout orchestration; runtime only guarantees per-scope atomicity.
- Patch/field-level rollback. Whole-config semantics only (ADR-017).

Problem statement
Current runtime config updates can be observed as partially applied when:
- multiple operators trigger applies back-to-back
- an apply attempt times out while runtime is still reconciling
- cache/scheduler subsystems read from different config sources during transition

This leads to “split knobs” within a single route/model scope: e.g., batching changed but cache policy not; or quantization profile toggled without required warmup/capacity gate.

Requirements
Functional
1) Serialize apply/rollback per scope key.
2) Activation must be atomic within the runtime for the scope:
   - requests must observe either version N or version N+1, not a mix
   - streaming requests that started under the previous version should continue under that version until completion (best-effort, see notes)
3) Apply must be idempotent:
   - repeated apply with same desired_version + idempotency_key should not re-run disruptive steps
4) Runtime must report a consistent status model back to control plane:
   - pending → preparing → activating → active OR failed
   - include failure reason + which stage failed

Reliability / safety
5) Lock must be lease-based (TTL) to recover from crashed workers.
6) Control plane must be able to “force unlock” only with elevated RBAC (optimize.config.rollback + breakglass) and should emit audit events.
7) Avoid global locks; do not block unrelated tenants/routes.
8) Updates should be safe under partial propagation: if some runtime instances apply and others fail, the scope should be marked degraded and rollback should remain possible.

Performance
9) Lock acquisition + activation should not add overhead to steady-state request path.
10) Apply should not require full process restart.

Proposed design
High-level: 1) acquire lock (lease), 2) stage config, 3) atomically swap active pointer, 4) release lock, 5) report status + metrics.

A) Lock/lease mechanism
- Lock storage: runtime-side “ApplyLock” held in the control plane (recommended) OR runtime coordinator service (if we can’t rely on control plane latency). Current plan per architecture thread: control plane lock table keyed by scope.
- Lease fields:
  - scope_key
  - lease_id (uuid)
  - holder (service name + instance id)
  - acquired_at
  - expires_at
  - last_renewed_at
  - operation: apply | rollback
  - desired_version_id
  - request_id / idempotency_key

- Semantics:
  - Acquire: conditional write (if no active lease or expired).
  - Renew: holder periodically renews (e.g., every 10s, TTL 60s).
  - Release: delete/mark released when operation completes.
  - If lease expires mid-operation: runtime should stop attempting activation and report “lease_lost” to control plane to avoid two operators both applying.

- Contention behavior:
  - If lock held: return 409 Conflict (or 423 Locked) from apply endpoint with current holder + expires_at so Console can render “apply already in progress”.
  - Optional: allow enqueueing at orchestration layer; runtime itself does not queue.

B) Atomic activation semantics inside runtime
We implement a “double-buffer + pointer swap” model per scope:
- Runtime maintains ConfigStore[scope] with:
  - active_version_id
  - active_config_blob (immutable snapshot)
  - staged_version_id
  - staged_config_blob
  - activation_epoch (monotonic int)

Apply steps:
1) Fetch config snapshot for desired_version_id (control plane) including resolved defaults.
2) Validate again at runtime boundary (cheap checks): schema version compatibility, quant profile existence, bounds on batch params. (Preflight validator is authoritative; runtime checks are defense-in-depth.)
3) Stage: load blob into staged_config_blob. Precompute any derived state (e.g., scheduler knobs, batching planner).
4) Activate atomically:
   - swap active pointer to staged blob in a single atomic write under scope mutex
   - bump activation_epoch
5) Post-activate hooks:
   - cache invalidation if required (see section D)
   - warmup if enabled (non-blocking; do not delay activation, but mark status “active_warming”)

Notes on request consistency:
- New requests should read active_config via an atomic pointer read.
- In-flight requests:
  - Best-effort “stickiness” to config captured at request start. For streaming, capture config pointer in request context.
  - We will not attempt to migrate an in-flight request mid-stream.

C) Status model + propagation
Runtime reports apply status per scope with granularity per runtime instance. Control plane aggregates into rollout status.
- Instance status payload:
  - scope_key
  - instance_id
  - operation_id
  - desired_version_id
  - stage: preparing|activating|active|failed|lease_lost
  - timestamps
  - failure_reason (string)

Aggregation rules (control plane):
- “Active” when >= quorum of instances (configurable per tier) have activated and none are in failed state OR failures below threshold.
- “Degraded” when some instances failed but quorum active.
- “Failed” when activation quorum not met within timeout.

D) Interactions with batching/KV cache/quantization
This ticket’s requirement is to avoid partial knob activation within a scope. Additional specifics:
- KV/prefix cache:
  - If config changes any cache key-space-affecting fields (e.g., kv_cache.enabled, prefix_cache.enabled, tokenizer revision), runtime must increment a cache namespace salt to prevent incorrect cache hits.
  - Cache invalidation should be non-blocking but immediate for new requests.
- Continuous batching:
  - Swapping batch.max_tokens_per_batch / max_batch_size should not tear down scheduler; instead update scheduler parameters atomically with config pointer swap.
  - For extreme decreases (guardrail), runtime may temporarily disable batching for that scope for 30s while reconciling (feature-flagged). Needs signoff from Sofia.
- Quantization profile swaps:
  - Must ensure model weights/profile already loaded or loadable.
  - Activation should fail fast if profile not present and cannot be loaded within timeout (to avoid partial ‘half-quantized’ state).

E) Rollback
Rollback is implemented as an apply with desired_version_id = prior version.
- Same lock key, same activation semantics.
- Rollback should prefer speed over warmup. Default: skip warmup and enable conservative scheduler settings for first 2 minutes (optional flag).

API/contract changes needed
- Apply/Rollback endpoints must include:
  - scope identifiers
  - desired_version_id
  - idempotency_key
  - requested_by (for audit correlation)
- Runtime needs endpoints/hooks to:
  - report per-instance activation status
  - query current active_version_id per scope (for drift detection)

Open questions
1) Do we need a separate “runtime local lock” in addition to control plane lease? Current proposal: scope mutex local for pointer swap only; lease is global serialization.
2) How to define quorum for Dedicated vs Hosted? Tentative:
   - Hosted: 90% of instances in cluster for that route/model
   - Dedicated: 100% (or allow 1 failure if HA pair)
   - Private: configurable; default 100%
3) Force unlock policy: require breakglass and incident/ticket link? PM + Security to confirm.

Acceptance criteria
- Concurrent apply/rollback attempts for same scope reliably result in only one proceeding (others receive Locked/Conflict response with active lease info).
- Runtime never exposes partial config updates within a scope (verified by integration test with deliberate delay between subsystem updates).
- Lease expiry recovery works: if holder dies, a new apply can proceed after TTL.
- Status reporting surfaces partial propagation vs full success, and Console can show “degraded / failed” clearly.
- Metrics emitted: config_apply_lock_acquire_latency, config_apply_lease_lost_total, config_activation_success_total, config_activation_failed_total (per scope labels).

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - lock acquisition/renew/release behaviors
  - atomic pointer swap with concurrent readers
- Integration tests (staging cluster):
  - two simultaneous applies → one wins; other gets 409
  - crash runtime worker mid-apply → lease expires; new apply succeeds; no split-brain
  - induced failure on 1 of N instances → aggregated state shows degraded; rollback allowed
- Chaos (optional):
  - inject network partition between control plane and subset of runtime instances; verify status shows stuck and lease eventually resolves

Updates / activity log
2025-01-17 (Mateo Alvarez)
- Created ticket. Pulled into P0 after incident thread showed manual rollback took ~40 minutes due to uncertainty about what actually propagated.

2025-01-22 (Omar El-Sayed)
- Drafted design for scope_key + lease fields; aligned with ENG-4823 idempotency key usage.

2025-01-27 (Sofia Ivanova)
- Review: pointer swap must update scheduler knobs in same critical section; do not allow a window where scheduler sees new batch size but old cache policy. Suggested representing derived scheduler params inside the immutable config snapshot.

2025-01-30 (Neha Kapoor)
- Review: require explicit “lease_lost” status to avoid silent split-brain; also want alerting on elevated lease_lost_total (ties to ENG-4828).

2025-02-03 (Chloe Martin)
- Needs: API response should include current active_version_id and current lease holder info so Console can render helpful UX. Added to contract notes.

2025-02-06 (Mateo Alvarez)
- Implementation mostly complete in PR-10479; requesting review from Noah Patel (correctness) and Jada Williams (rollout orchestration expectations). Remaining: force-unlock admin path (may go into ENG-4823 follow-up) and finalize quorum defaults by tier.
